still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived. Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit, and Medicare reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 28.8% ever-used minus 19.6% current = 9.2% of adults who used the drugs and are off now. About 55% of current users are on a second or later course (10.8 points), and 2.2 points cycled and are off again, so 13.0 / 28.8 ≈ 45% of ever-users have cycled. The other ~7.0 points stopped once and have not restarted. This is consistent with one-year persistence still near one-third on weekly and oral products (monthly clinic-administered MariTide runs ~60% at 12 months inside employer tracks) and 36–47% restarting within a year. Age check: 0.20×11 + 0.33×19.5 + 0.24×29.5 + 0.23×17 = 2.2 + 6.4 + 7.1 + 3.9 ≈ 19.6. Income thirds average ~19.7, bracketing the national figure. About 19.6% of ~272M adults is ~53.3M users. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~26% (~13.9M, flat in absolute terms while users grew), Medicare ~21% (~11.2M), Medicaid ~6% (~3.2M), legitimate cash (TrumpRx/direct/telehealth) ~33% (~17.6M, including ~1.3M on telehealth 'calm' microdose plans), imported or counterfeit ~14% (~7.5M, up from ~5.2M). The bottom third's gain (12 → 14) comes almost entirely from gray-market product, which makes it the least stable use in the country. Adult obesity is ~33.4%. Roughly 23% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and adults 65+ without CVD codes. Pediatric: ~1.2% of under-18s are on a drug, ~2.6% of 12–17s. About 0.25% of 6–11s take daily liraglutide, and new under-12 starts fell roughly a third after the Feb 2032 growth communication. About 4.5M children under 18 live with a parent who has regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~11.2M users only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes, all behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 11.2M × ~$235 average net/month × 12 ≈ $31.6B a year in gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up. Of that, the dementia route (~1.9M × ~$245 × 12) ≈ $5.6B. It grew within the existing label after the June 2031 CRL kept the non-CVD extension off the market. Medicaid: 7 states still cover weight-loss use, down from 9 (Kentucky and New Mexico dropped it in 2031 budgets), and ~3.2M Medicaid users are mostly on diabetes codes. Two state programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide sells for $4–30 a month across 100+ brands. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials sell for $20–60 in markets without enforceable patents. Canadian and Brazilian generics run CAD 50–85 and BRL 180–300. India and China supply roughly two-thirds of the world's incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Employers covering weight management fell from 36% to 30% (Business Group on Health, Nov 2031). Another ~12% cover only through monitored metabolic tracks, which now hold ~5.6M enrollees, all inside the ~13.9M commercial users. ~3.9M of them are on clinic-administered MariTide. In May 2031 Amgen cut MariTide's direct cash price $299 → $249 and signed PBM deals making it the preferred track product. Novo and Lilly answered by cutting TrumpRx maintenance prices: Wegovy pill $249 → $199, Foundayo $149–229, injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $249–299. Starting oral doses stay $149. Retatrutide list is $1,299, ~$399 cash direct. Amycretin (approved Dec 2030) is $1,249 list, mostly on commercial formularies with prior authorisation. Total MariTide users ~4.6M. Orals are ~46% of users. The gray market is now ~7.5M users and includes Indian vials, Chinese tirzepatide analogues, counterfeit serialised pens with cloned codes, and 'monthly' depot vials that do not exist in any approved form. Telegram shops and WhatsApp reseller networks now sell more than social storefronts.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Dec 2030)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; label updated Apr 2032 with growth-monitoring language)

reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide; confirmatory trial ongoing). The extension to 60+ without CVD received a Complete Response Letter in Jun 2031
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm' and 'focus' microdosing sold through telehealth subscriptions (low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo), ~1.3M subscribers
alcohol reduction via telehealth and employer EAPs (oral semaglutide AUD phase 3 read out positive in 2031; sNDA filed Jan 2032, decision 2033)
dementia-prevention use by 50–70-year-olds without CVD, cash-paid, which grew after the CRL as people bypassed the label
microdosing for 'steadiness' recommended by employer wellness coaches
semaglutide in under-12s with severe obesity (off-label; it fell after the Feb 2032 communication)
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Amycretin, under review since Oct 2029, was approved Dec 2030 for chronic weight management at ~22% weight loss. It is a new product, not a new indication. Lilly's tirzepatide dementia sNDA for adults 60+ without CVD got a CRL in Jun 2031: the FDA wanted confirmatory-trial data and a fracture/EPI risk-mitigation plan, and the confirmatory trial reads out no earlier than 2033. So new_indications is 'none'. Oral semaglutide for AUD read out positive in phase 3 (2031) and was filed Jan 2032, with no decision before 2033. The monthly driver is realised through MariTide's scale-up (~4.6M users) and clinic administration inside employer tracks. No implant exists; implant programmes are in phase 1 to early phase 2 and are not on the market. Bimagrumab-type muscle adjuncts read out phase 3 in 2031 with modest lean-mass preservation, were filed in Jul 2032 and are not approved. No oral matches tirzepatide. The global incretin market is ~$165B (2031). US net prices drift down 3–5% a year and brands hold above ~$150.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside clinic-administered tracks. MariTide's early vomiting has eased with slower titration. Chronic diarrhoea in long-term users is now routinely worked up for EPI.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
Still no causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Litigation now centres on exocrine insufficiency.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; new MDL filings consolidated in 2031 on EPI claims.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare cohort hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 in users 65+ after more than 2 years, ~1.45 after three or more cycles, and is compounded in EPI patients by vitamin D/K malabsorption. The fracture data were central to the June 2031 dementia CRL.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning (Jul 2028) retained; DXA code in use; resistance-training counselling statement on retatrutide and amycretin labels.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal in adults. The pediatric psychiatric signal concerns restrictive eating, not suicidality.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~7–8% of users vs ~3% of controls, ~10% on retatrutide. It is dose-related. The milder 'evenness' that most users report is now the selling point of telehealth calm plans. No randomised data; the FDA postmarketing observational study is due 2033.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling. FDA sent untitled letters to two telehealth platforms over implied anxiety and focus claims (2031); no enforcement followed.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Gray-market users who stop after bad batches regain fastest.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins the chronic-therapy framing and adherence monitoring.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users. Fat-soluble deficiency is tied to EPI. Low ferritin is reported in adolescent girls on semaglutide.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language added to semaglutide and tirzepatide labels (2031).

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: A third replication (UK CPRD, 2031) confirmed ~2× EPI incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years). Partial recovery of faecal elastase was seen in about half of people who stopped for 12+ months. Tirzepatide data at 5+ years are emerging, with a smaller and non-significant excess so far.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling added in Mar 2031 (EPI warning; faecal elastase testing for persistent diarrhoea). EMA PRAC concluded with similar wording. Tirzepatide is under continued review.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. The first pediatric developmental signal arrived in 2032 (see next entry). Cycling effects on bone and pancreas remain poorly characterised.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone-density and growth postmarketing requirements continue; the interim growth analysis was published early.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~23,000 by mid-2032. In Sep 2031 CDC linked non-sterile imported vials to ~640 nontuberculous mycobacterial skin and soft-tissue infections across 22 states, plus a separate cluster of Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials at 3–5× labelled concentration (~380 ED visits for intractable vomiting and dehydration, 11 deaths in total across both clusters). Cloned serial codes now defeat the pen authentication scans. Poison-centre calls are ~5× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alert extended to named Chinese API makers. CBP seizures are up ~2.5× from 2030. Personal-importation enforcement is still weak, and no federal or state statute changed.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The liraglutide 6–11 PMR interim analysis (n≈2,900, Jan 2032) found height velocity ~0.7 cm/year below expected in children who were prepubertal at start, with no catch-up yet observed at 24 months. A Swedish adolescent registry (started at 12–14 on semaglutide, 2023–2029) found later onset of pubertal staging in boys and an ARFID/restrictive-eating diagnosis HR of ~1.8 (absolute ~6 vs ~3.3 per 1,000 person-years). It is unclear how much of this is drug, how much caloric deficit and how much confounding by severity. Final adult height is unknown and will not be known for years.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (Feb 2032). The liraglutide 6–11 label was updated (Apr 2032) with growth-velocity monitoring every 6 months, Tanner staging and eating-disorder screening. The AAP issued interim guidance favouring lifestyle-first for prepubertal children. No age restriction was imposed. EMA review opened.

food_and_beverage.state: About 36% of US households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~9–11% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~9%. Dollar sales are flat because of price and premium mix. The class split in the aisle is now a formal strategy: Kroger and Albertsons plan stores by zip-code user density, with 'GLP-1 friendly' protein bays in upper-income suburbs and value packs and private label in lower-income areas. PepsiCo and Mondelez have spun premium protein lines into separate brands. Whey prices eased as capacity came online; pea protein is still tight.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~12–13% from 2025 and beer ~8%. Losses concentrate among heavy drinkers, now also targeted by telehealth calm plans that bundle alcohol reduction. Diageo sold two US whiskey brands. Midwestern mid-sized-city bar closures continue. Non-alcoholic and functional 'calm' drinks grow but are small.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. Casual-dining checks are smaller. Darden and Brinker run portion-tiered menus. QSR value menus grow in lower-income markets where gray-market users regain. Buffets are now a niche category.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Growth is in premium structured athletic wear and in tailoring for 'lifted' bodies. Resale, stretch and rental serve cyclers and regainers. Size runs are now set by store zip code at the mass retailers.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Premium DXA-plus-coaching memberships run $250–400 a month. Budget chains sell $39 'lean-mass' add-ons. Employer metabolic tracks bundle clinic MariTide visits with InBody scans. Pediatric weight programmes lost enrolment after the growth communication, while family strength gyms gained.

insurance.state: Employer weight-loss coverage is at 30%. Pharmacy trend ~+6% as flat-net deals and the MariTide PBM preference offset volume. Adherence differentials have spread to more mid-sized self-insured firms, which use clinic administration records. Part D premiums rose again in 2032, partly on incretin spend. Pediatric prior authorisation now requires growth charts.

pharma.state: Lilly, Novo, Amgen and Boehringer share the branded US market. Amgen's MariTide grew fastest on employer-track volume. Lilly's dementia growth slowed after the CRL. Novo leans on orals and the Medicare price, with semaglutide's EPI label weighing on long-term persistence. Counterfeit defence spending is in the hundreds of millions. Indian and Chinese makers dominate global volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Body shape reads as income, and now also as how you are paid. Lean with visible muscle means covered, scanned and coached. Thin and soft with a monthly clinic bruise means an employer track. Thin with a sallow look means cash or mail-order. Regained after 50 means lost coverage or a bad batch. Among the upper tier, a child's growth chart has joined the parent's DXA as a status document.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle is the class uniform. In Charlotte and Austin the lean-mass percentage is office gossip, and 'off-drug lean' (people who stopped at goal and held it with coaching) is the newest elite boast. On the Columbus logistics corridor the plant-clinic body is thin without muscle. In Memphis and the Mississippi Delta, where gray-market use rose fastest, the visible body is the cycler, and you can read the batch history in the face. Upper-income parents in Bethesda and Plano are quietly pulling prepubertal children off liraglutide or switching to 'lifestyle-first' programmes after the growth communication. Medicaid-covered children who were added late are less likely to be monitored that closely.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter. Protein remains a hospitality marker. The Bread Alone fasting network claims ~650 congregations and has added a youth ministry framed around the pediatric findings. School-lunch debates have shifted from accommodating medicated children to whether schools should report weight at all.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'Lean-mass verified' badges remain a premium app tier. Some apps now let users tag 'on a calm plan'. Couples negotiate around the monthly shot date, and therapists report that one partner's calm subscription is a new kind of mismatch: one person finds the other flat and is told the flatness is something they pay for.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: In the upper tier, appetite and craving are noise that a subscription manages. In lower-income communities appetite signals lost access, or is defended as pride. The counter-movement remains split. Unmuted argues about class and the calm industry, the MAHA wing has seized on the children's growth data, and fat-acceptance revivalists stay apart from both.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~7–8% of users vs ~3% of controls, ~10% on retatrutide. About 1.3M people pay for telehealth 'calm' and 'focus' plans: low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo, $149–199 a month through TrumpRx-priced fills plus a $39–59 platform fee. They are buying the mild evenness most users report, and the anhedonia rate among them at low doses is unknown.
interior_life.framing: Telehealth platforms sell it as a feature: 'quiet the noise', 'craving-free focus', 'calm you can schedule'. Manufacturers avoid those words and say 'food noise'. HR still calls it steadiness. Clinicians call it a dose-related side effect. Unmuted calls it a sedative sold back to the people it was first prescribed to.
interior_life.effect_on_work: ~5.6M employees are in adherence-verified tracks, ~3.9M of them on clinic-administered MariTide. Shift-lead promotions in Columbus-corridor logistics and national call centres informally favour enrollees. In upper-tier firms nobody monitors anything; staff buy calm plans themselves and list 'focus protocol' beside sleep tracking. The two EEOC ADA charges remain unresolved at the end of 2032.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Flat' fiction has competition from 'off' memoir: accounts of stopping and feeling everything return. Unmuted off nights run in Detroit, Baltimore and now Memphis. Sportsbook wagering per active account is down again in insured suburbs. Streaming platforms report calm-plan subscribers favour slow 'ambient' series, and some marketers now target that segment.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: The monthly shot date organises couples' calendars. Desire mismatch is the most common presenting complaint at some couples' practices. Therapists see more 'parallel lives' and a new pattern: partners who take a calm plan to cope with the other's flatness.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The adherence-premium coalition remains stalled and no state acted. The live political argument moved to children, where MAHA-aligned legislators hold hearings on the growth data without passing bills, and to calm marketing, where FDA untitled letters produced headlines but no rules. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence. Medicated and regained voters are increasingly sorted by zip code.

state.regulatory_posture: Routine and permissive. FDA approved amycretin, issued a CRL on the dementia extension, added EPI and micronutrient labelling to semaglutide, issued the pediatric growth communication and label update, and sent untitled letters over calm-plan marketing without enforcement. No state legislature or agency acted, Illinois's ban is still the only one, and Congress created no coverage, mandate or premium rule.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: None new. TrumpRx operates on manufacturer-set prices. The Medicare Bridge pilot was not revived. The 2027 tri-agency 30% wellness guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in law, deeper in practice. Clinic administration records for monthly injections, PBM fills and telehealth app logs flow to wellness vendors under consent. Telehealth calm platforms collect mood check-ins and sell de-identified 'focus' cohorts to employer-benefit brokers. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE rules are unchanged. The Army recruit oral pilot continues without expansion. DOT still has not ruled on off-label alcohol-reduction use, or now calm-plan use, among commercial drivers.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply about two-thirds of world incretin volume. US–India talks still list CBP mail enforcement without agreement. The FDA named Chinese API makers in the 2031 import-alert extension, and Beijing protested. The US cash-to-Indian-generic price gap is ~40–50×.

events.event: Telehealth platform Level launches 'Quiet', a $59-a-month calm-and-focus subscription built on low-dose oral semaglutide filled at TrumpRx prices; with copycats, calm plans pass 1.3 million subscribers by mid-2032 despite FDA untitled letters

Amgen cuts MariTide's direct cash price to $249 and wins PBM preference as the clinic-administered product in employer metabolic tracks; Novo and Lilly cut TrumpRx maintenance prices to $199–299 within weeks

FDA issues a Complete Response Letter on Lilly's bid to extend tirzepatide's dementia-risk claim to adults 60+ without heart disease, citing fracture and pancreatic data and the unfinished confirmatory trial

CDC links non-sterile imported vials to ~640 mycobacterial infections in 22 states, and super-concentrated Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials to hundreds of ER visits; 11 deaths in total, while CBP seizures run 2.5× 2030 levels
Business Group on Health survey finds only 30% of employers still cover weight-loss drugs, while monitored metabolic tracks grow to 5.6 million enrollees

FDA safety communication reports slower height growth in children who started liraglutide before puberty and a Swedish registry links early adolescent semaglutide to later puberty and restrictive eating; growth-monitoring labelling follows in April

open_tensions: Children who started incretins before puberty are growing ~0.7 cm a year more slowly, and no one knows their final adult height. The label now says measure them, not stop, and new starts fell mostly in the households most able to monitor.

Calm is now a product. 1.3 million people buy the mild blunting that the anhedonia cohort counts as harm at higher doses. Regulators have sent letters and nothing more, and employers are starting to buy 'focus' cohorts.

7.5 million Americans take mail-order or counterfeit product, and the bottom third's rising use rests on vials that infected hundreds and overdosed hundreds more in 2031. Each bad batch converts users into regainers.

The dementia CRL pushed prevention-minded 60-year-olds toward cash and gray channels, the group with the highest fracture and EPI exposure, while Part D premiums keep rising on incretin spend under the existing label.

prose.headline: Calm, Sold Monthly: America Buys a Quieter Mind as Its Medicated Children Start Coming Up Short
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 about one American adult in five takes an incretin drug, roughly fifty-three million people, and nearly three in ten have tried one. The number rose by two points in two years, about as fast as the cheapest channels allowed. Who pays changed faster. Only 30 percent of employers still cover the drugs for weight loss. Most that remain use monitored metabolic tracks, where a nurse at the plant clinic gives a monthly shot of Amgen's MariTide and the record goes straight to the wellness vendor. Five and a half million workers sit in those programmes. Their premiums are lower if the record is complete.

Prices fell the way manufacturers chose. In 2031 Amgen cut MariTide to $249 a month in cash and won preferred status with the benefit managers. Novo and Lilly matched within weeks, bringing maintenance prices in the government's cash channel down to $199 for the Wegovy pill and below $300 for the injectables. Starting pills are still $149. The $1,349 list price is still on the box. Amycretin, approved at the end of 2030, joined the formularies behind prior authorisation.

The newest market is not for weight at all. In March 2031 a telehealth company began selling Quiet, a low-dose semaglutide subscription promising calm and focus without cravings, and within a year more than a million people subscribed to it or its imitators. The FDA sent letters and took no further action. The pills are legal and prescribed, and the advertising carefully says 'noise' and never 'anxiety'. The cohort that counts one heavy user in thirteen losing a real share of pleasure has not studied people on low doses. The subscribers are mostly salaried, mostly urban and mostly sure it is working.

The drug did not get the new use that mattered most. In June 2031 the FDA declined to extend tirzepatide's dementia claim to older adults without heart disease, citing hip fractures and the pancreatic finding that by then had its own warning on semaglutide's label. Many of those people buy it anyway, for cash or by mail.

The mail is heavier than before. About seven and a half million Americans now use Indian vials, Chinese tirzepatide copies or counterfeit pens with cloned serial codes. In 2031 non-sterile vials gave hundreds of people mycobacterial skin infections. Other vials held three to five times the labelled dose and sent hundreds more to emergency rooms. Eleven people died. Seizures more than doubled, and the packages kept coming. Almost all of the bottom third's new users came through this channel, and they stop most abruptly.

In February 2032 the children's numbers arrived. An early look at the growth study attached to liraglutide's approval for six-to-eleven-year-olds found that children who started before puberty were growing about seven-tenths of a centimetre a year more slowly than expected. A Swedish registry linked early teenage semaglutide to later puberty in boys and more restrictive eating. The FDA told doctors to measure height every six months and screen for eating disorders. It did not tell them to stop. Some parents in Bethesda and Plano took their children off quietly. In families who came to the drug late, through Medicaid, fewer people are watching the chart.

The sorting of bodies continues. In Charlotte and Austin the prized body is lifted and scanned, and the newest boast is having stopped at goal and held it with a coach. Along the Columbus freight corridor the body is thin and soft and bruised once a month at the clinic. In Memphis, where gray-market use rose fastest, the visible body is the cycler's. No state acted, Congress did nothing and the complaints at the EEOC remain undecided. From a distance the country looks calmer. Some of that calm is a subscription.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Dana Okafor clocks in at 5:52 at the distribution centre in Groveport, Ohio, eight minutes early, because the third Tuesday is clinic day. The nurse calls her name at 10:15. Left thigh this month. A scan of her badge, the MariTide pen, a sticker on her wellness card. Her premium stays at the track rate, ninety-one dollars a pay period less than Marisol's on the next line, who didn't enroll.

She eats half a turkey wrap at lunch and puts the other half in her locker for later. She won't want it later.

At four she picks up Ayo, ten, from school and drives him to the pediatric endocrinologist in Dublin. He's been on generic liraglutide for two years, a daily pen in the bathroom drawer next to her old one. The nurse measures him twice. The doctor turns the screen toward her: the curve and the dotted line under it. Not alarming, she says. We'll check again in six months. There's a handout, three pages, from the FDA.

In the parking lot Dana reads the first paragraph and folds it into her purse.

Her sister texts from Memphis: a photo of a vial with Hindi on the label and a question mark. Dana types don't, deletes it, and types is it from the same guy?

At home Ayo asks if he has to keep taking it. She says she'll ask his dad. He doesn't eat his rice.

After he's asleep she scrolls past an ad for Quiet: a woman on a balcony, eyes closed, Calm you can schedule. Dana closes the app. She feels fine. She feels, she thinks, about the same as always.
